title: Cancellation Notice Windows and Charge Percentages by Catering Service Level
content:
Three figures are printed against each service level of the Corporate Catering Service Agreement for the purposes of a cancelled order: the hours of notice before service at which a cancellation carries no charge, the charge for a cancellation made inside that free window but before the service day, and the charge for a cancellation made on the service day itself. The two charges are percentages of order value.

| Service level | Free-cancellation notice | Within-notice percentage | Same-day percentage |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Drop-Off Catering Account | 24 hours | 25.0 per cent | 75.0 per cent |
| Delivered Buffet Account | 48 hours | 35.0 per cent | 85.0 per cent |
| Attended Buffet Account | 72 hours | 50.0 per cent | 100.0 per cent |
| Staffed Full-Service Catering Account | 96 hours | 60.0 per cent | 100.0 per cent |
| Executive Hospitality Catering Account | 72 hours | 65.0 per cent | 100.0 per cent |
| Campus Catering Master Account | 120 hours | 55.0 per cent | 100.0 per cent |

The same-day percentage reaches 100.0 per cent at the Attended Buffet Account and stands there for every level above it, so from that level upward a cancellation on the service day leaves nothing of the order value unrecovered. The within-notice percentage does not rise in step: it peaks at 65.0 per cent on the Executive Hospitality Catering Account and stands at 55.0 per cent on the Campus Catering Master Account, whose free-cancellation window of 120 hours is the longest in the schedule.
